inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated cash-flow statement, 'Share-based payments' EUR 202m (SU.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:39823); FY2024 EUR 233m. No separate equity-award tax line (French performance-share plans are settled from treasury shares; EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis). Interest income EUR 152m is NOT stripped: the group is net-debt (EUR 15.4bn), so gross cash is netted against debt in the bridge and the unlevered build is before all interest.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:39:57Z regular close (Euronext Paris); latest close as of the valuation date
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-30 (net debt EUR 15,360m, H1 2026 results presentation p.39); gross cash/debt split only disclosed at 2025-12-31 (cash 4,634 / financial liabilities 17,880 excl. IFRS 16 leases 1,554); total_debt here = June-26 net debt + Dec-25 cash, a derived figure
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted ex-convertibles: 562.2m weighted shares net of treasury (577.1m issued less ~14.9m treasury) + 2.3m dilutive performance shares (FY2025 URD note 20.2). The 6.05m shares from OCEANE convertibles are EXCLUDED because the bonds sit inside financial liabilities / net debt (counting both would double-charge). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The H1-26 EUR 0.6bn buyback (~2.5m shares) is not yet netted, which is mildly conservative.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity 8.3% = 10y Bund ~2.8% (Oct-2026) + beta 1.1 x ERP 5.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.6% (A/A2-rated EUR bonds) -> 2.7% after 24% tax. Weights ~85/15 on today's market cap (EUR ~131bn) against pro-forma net debt of ~EUR 29bn once Cognite, AiDASH and the debt-funded part of PTC close -> WACC 7.3-7.6%; 7.5% used. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality, data-centre concentration and integration risk are charged in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full IFRS 16 payment (2026 maturity EUR 292m principal + ~EUR 50m interest = 0.85% of revenue) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; IFRS 16 debt (EUR 1,554m at Dec-25) EXCLUDED from net debt (Schneider's own net-debt definition also excludes it); D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (~3.4% vs 4.1% total).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI (FY2025 NCI profit share EUR 188m, book EUR 256m - mostly the Delixi China LV JV and Motivair 25%) deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 15x NCI profit (EUR 2.8bn). Book value is not used because it badly understates Delixi.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: electrical distribution, industrial automation, software). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US industrial) with the adaptations file: EUR WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, SBC-light market. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). EBITDA DEFINITION: the engine's ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA BEFORE SBC and AFTER a recurring restructuring allowance (~0.5% of revenue; FY2025 restructuring EUR 287m = 0.7%, FY2024 0.4%). FY2025 anchor: adj EBITA 18.7% + depreciation 2.2% + SBC 0.5% - restructuring 0.4% = 20.9%; the engine then deducts SBC (0.55%) and the lease charge (0.85%) explicitly. FY2026 (year 1) follows the 16-Oct-2026 guidance: organic revenue +12-14%, FX -EUR 300-400m, scope -EUR 50m -> ~+12% reported; adj EBITA margin +100-120bps organic -> pre-SBC EBITDA ~22.0%. M&A: the pending Cognite ($3.1bn), AiDASH and PTC ($22.6bn, close ~Q3 2027) deals are EXCLUDED from the flows (as they are from guidance). Cognite/AiDASH are treated as value-neutral (price ~ fair value, debt funded). PTC is carried in the equity bridge as an expected NPV to Schneider shareholders (see equity_bridge). TIMING: FY0 = FY2025 with the June-2026 balance sheet; year-1 (FY2026) flows include H1-26 FCF of EUR 1.6bn already inside June net debt, while the EUR 2.4bn May dividend and EUR 0.6bn buyback have already left - net effect roughly a wash (<EUR 3/share). SHAREHOLDERS' EQUITY: the FY2025 fall to EUR 24,199m from 30,489m is as reported in the consolidated balance sheet (SU.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:36650), not a parse error; it is far larger than the net income +4.2bn / dividends -2.2bn / buyback -0.3bn bridge and is presumably dominated by FX translation losses on USD/INR/CNY net assets and NCI/put-option movements. It does not enter the DCF (which uses net debt), but it makes the equity CAGR useless as a growth proxy, so growth selection uses revenue/market growth instead. Buybacks: the company IS funding the flat count (EUR 341m FY25, EUR 0.6bn H1-26 incl. commitment) so the flat-count convention is paid for.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at 15x FY2025 NCI profit share (EUR 188m)
equity_bridge.note: Delixi China LV JV + Motivair 25%; book value EUR 256m understates. Charged once here, flows left 100% consolidated. SU.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:40815

equity_bridge.item: PTC acquisition: expected NPV to Schneider shareholders
equity_bridge.note: $205/share for ~110m PTC shares vs ~$140 undisturbed (late Sep-2026 average; PTC closed $144.03 on 2-Oct before the 5-Oct announcement) = ~$7.2bn premium = EUR 6.4bn at EURUSD 1.122 (Yahoo, 2026-10-25). Credited: EUR 250m run-rate synergies by year 3 post-close (~2030), after 24% tax = EUR 190m, capitalised at WACC-g 5.0% = EUR 3.8bn in 2030, discounted 4 years at 7.5% = EUR 2.85bn, less ~EUR 0.3bn after-tax integration one-offs -> EUR 2.55bn. Net -EUR 3.85bn x ~85% completion probability (PTC shareholder + multi-jurisdiction antitrust approvals) = -EUR 3.3bn. No revenue-synergy credit; no deduction for the equity-funding component (issuance at market is value-neutral once the deal cost is charged here).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: revenue 5yr CAGR 9.8% (FY2020-25, SBC-adjusted FCF 4.8%/12.5%) tempered to the 6-7% addressable-market CAGR Schneider cites to 2030; near-term guided +12-14% organic. Equity CAGR rejected as the primary source (see growth_divergence_warning).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR -1.6% diverges >30% from revenue (5.5%) and EPS (6.0%). Cause: the FY2025 shareholders' equity fell to EUR 24,199m from 30,489m as reported (consolidated balance sheet, SU.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:36650) - a move far larger than the earnings/dividend/buyback bridge, presumably FX translation on USD/INR/CNY net assets plus NCI/put-option effects. Reported, but not used for growth selection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped: net-debt company). FY2020 3,473 / FY2022 3,077 / FY2025 4,386 (EUR m). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.5pp of each other: SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and stable, so it is not eating the FCF growth. FY2025 reported FCF carried a one-off EUR 207m French competition fine payment; FY2022 was a working-capital trough (supply-chain inventory build), which flatters the 3yr CAGR.

base.narrative: FY2026 at the midpoint of the raised guidance (~+12% reported after FX/scope); data-centre demand normalises from triple-digit to strong double-digit growth through 2028 while Buildings/Industry/Infrastructure grow mid-single-digit, so group growth decelerates 8% -> 3% over the decade toward the 6-7% market CAGR and then below it. Adj EBITA margin expands ~50bps/yr to ~21% by 2030 (pre-SBC EBITDA 23.5%) on mix (software/services 'Digital Flywheel'), pricing and SFC leverage, then holds. Capex stays above D&A (capacity for liquid cooling, Dunkirk power modules, regionalisation). Working capital consumes 8c per euro of growth (manufacturer: receivables + inventory > payables). Tax 24% per the 23-25% ETR guidance.

bull.narrative: AI-factory build-out runs through 2029 with Schneider's grid-to-chip-to-chiller position (800VDC, Motivair liquid cooling, 20 of the top hyperscalers/colos) taking share; Industrial Automation recovers to high-single-digit growth; US and India lead. Group growth stays double-digit through 2028 and FY2026 lands at the top of guidance. Mix shift toward software/services and continued SFC-ratio gains take adj EBITA toward ~22.5% (pre-SBC EBITDA 25%), the level of the best-in-class electrical peers. Heavier capacity capex is the price of the share gains. Terminal growth 3.0% for a structurally growing electrification market.

bear.narrative: FY2026 still lands near the bottom of guidance because nine months are banked, but hyperscaler capex digests in 2027-28: Data Center & Networks (30% of orders) falls ~25% from peak, Systems backlog converts at lower margin, and Buildings/Residential stays soft in Europe, so group revenue is flat-to-down for two years before resuming ~3% growth. Price/cost turns negative (raw materials, tariffs, under-absorption of the new liquid-cooling and power-module capacity), adj EBITA compresses ~150bps to ~18% before a slow recovery to ~19%. Management is simultaneously integrating Motivair, Planon, Cognite, AiDASH and PTC, so cost actions lag. Working-capital release in the downturn and capex cuts cushion FCF. Terminal growth 2.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-year at midpoint, then a decade of deceleration from 8% to 3% as the data-centre supercycle normalises into the 6-7% electrification market; adj EBITA margin reaches ~21% by 2030 and holds; PTC carried as a modestly value-destructive deal (premium > PV of synergies) in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-factory capex sustains through 2029 with share gains from the integrated power + liquid-cooling + software offer; double-digit growth through 2028, adj EBITA toward 22.5%, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex digestion in 2027-28 takes Data Center & Networks down ~25% from peak; two flat-to-down years, ~150bps margin compression on under-absorbed capacity and price/cost, slow recovery to ~19% adj EBITA, while five acquisitions are integrated at once.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised: 30% of orders now come from one end-market (Data Center & Networks) whose customers' capex is discretionary and lumpy, and the group is integrating five acquisitions concurrently including its largest ever at a 42% premium, which is exactly the setup in which a demand air-pocket becomes a margin event. Bull trimmed: the bull case needs three independent things to go right at once (AI capex sustained through 2029, margin expansion to best-in-class 22.5% adj EBITA, and PTC synergies delivered on time). The balance sheet (A/A2, ~1.6x ND/EBITDA pre-deals, ~2.3x pro-forma) carries no solvency risk, so bear is not pushed higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a standalone Schneider (excluding the unclosed PTC, Cognite and AiDASH deals from the flows), with SBC fully expensed, IFRS 16 leases charged as an operating cost, NCI deducted once at a fair multiple, and the PTC deal carried in the bridge at its expected NPV to Schneider shareholders rather than pro-forma'd into the flows on an unknown funding mix. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% and 20x year-10 owner FCF (the cap binds marginally). One WACC across scenarios; risk is priced in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Data-centre capex cycle: 30% of orders; a 25% peak-to-trough in that end-market is the bear case and the single largest driver of the bear/base gap

PTC deal: the -EUR 3.3bn bridge item assumes ~85% completion and EUR 250m synergies; if the deal breaks the item reverses to ~zero (+EUR 6/share), if synergies are not delivered it roughly doubles (-EUR 6/share more); PTC's own revenue, FCF and the equity-funding share count are not yet in the model and must be added at closing
Terminal value is ~65% of EV and the 20x cap binds: a 1pp change in WACC moves the base IV by roughly 15-20%
Margin trajectory: the base assumes adj EBITA ~21% by 2030 (from 18.7% FY25); if price/cost (raw materials, tariffs) turns negative the base converges on the bear path
FX: >80% of revenue is non-EUR (USD EUR 15bn); 10% EUR appreciation vs USD = -EUR 427m adj EBITA per management, not separately modelled
Shareholders' equity fell EUR 6.3bn in FY2025 as reported (FX translation / NCI effects, not bridged here); it does not enter the DCF but distorts the equity CAGR and any P/B-based screen
